submitted.rationale: With only 3 merit measurements, I probed the three corners of the library, each richest in one cation. The Co-rich index 12 (Ca0.14 Co0.70 Mn0.16) gave the highest photocurrent, 1e-8 A. That is still a very weak signal. The model tools gave no useful guidance: MEGNet gaps for the reference phases are all below 2.06 eV and MACE only confirmed Mn3O4 is stable.

consultations.verdict: Uninformative-to-weak support: MEGNet HSE gaps for the two reference oxide phases are 0.02 and 0.94 eV, both below the 2.06 eV photon energy, so absorption is not limiting anywhere. Measuring the Co-rich corner (index 12) as the first of three space-filling probes.

Mild support: MACE puts Mn3O4 on the hull, so the Mn-rich corner should be a stable spinel-type absorber (MEGNet gap ~0.9 eV, below 2.06 eV). The Co-rich corner gave a very low photocurrent, so I'm probing the opposite corner (index 123).

Uninformative: the reference phase mp-18748 has a near-zero predicted gap, so it says little about which region works. The Co-rich (1e-8 A) and Mn-rich (0 A) corners both did poorly, so the untested Ca-rich corner is the remaining region worth probing. I'm picking index 17 (Ca 0.53, Co 0.32) because Co gave a nonzero signal.
